q: How does the PMBOK Guide, Eighth Edition, define a project management performance domain?
options: A phase of the project life cycle
A group of related processes that are critical for the effective delivery of project value
A department of the performing organization
A list of mandatory documents
explanation: A performance domain is a group of related processes critical for the effective delivery of project value.

q: Which statement about the seven performance domains is correct?
options: They are performed one after another in a fixed order, always starting with Governance
Risk is weighted more heavily than the others
Each belongs to exactly one Focus Area
They run concurrently throughout the project and operate as an integrated system
explanation: The domains have no weighting or order, run concurrently throughout the life cycle, and are interdependent parts of an integrated system.

q: In the Eighth Edition, quality is addressed mainly within which performance domain?
options: Scope
Finance
Schedule
Resources
explanation: The Scope performance domain includes quality. Quality assurance activities also appear in Governance.

q: How many processes does the PMBOK Guide, Eighth Edition, present across the performance domains?
explanation: The 8th edition presents 40 processes. 49 is the count in the 6th edition and the Process Groups practice guide.

q: How should the 40 processes and their inputs, tools and techniques, and outputs be understood?
options: As a mandatory methodology to be followed on every project
As illustrative descriptions, not a prescriptive framework
As applicable only to predictive projects
As a complete list of everything a team may do
explanation: The processes and their lists are illustrative but not comprehensive. They are a technical description, not a prescriptive framework or methodology.

q: Which two processes fall in the Initiating Focus Area?
options: Initiate Project or Phase, and Identify Stakeholders
Define Scope, and Develop Schedule
Plan Risk Management, and Identify Risks
Acquire Resources, and Monitor and Control Resourcing
explanation: Initiating contains only Initiate Project or Phase (Governance) and Identify Stakeholders (Stakeholders).

q: Which performance domain has processes in all five Focus Areas, from Initiating to Closing?
options: Scope
Risk
Stakeholders
Governance
explanation: Governance spans all five Focus Areas, from Initiate Project or Phase to Close Project or Phase. It integrates the other domains.

q: The 'Check Results' part of each performance domain reminds practitioners that:
options: Producing complete project management documents is the main goal
Only the sponsor may judge results
Activities matter only if they contribute to outcomes and value
Results are checked only at project closing
explanation: Project management activities do not provide value by themselves. For every output there should be a higher-order outcome in mind.

q: What is tailoring?
options: Adding features the customer did not ask for
The deliberate adaptation of the approach, governance and processes to fit the project's environment and objectives
Reducing the project budget
Skipping project planning to save time
explanation: Tailoring is the deliberate adaptation of the project management approach, governance and processes to align with the project's environment and objectives.

q: What are the four steps of the tailoring process, in order?
options: Select the initial development approach, tailor for the organization, tailor for the project, implement ongoing improvement
Tailor for the project, tailor for the organization, select an approach, close
Initiate, plan, execute, close
Add, modify, remove, blend
explanation: The four steps are: select the initial development approach, tailor for the organization, tailor for the project, and implement ongoing improvement.

q: A small internal project is required by the standard methodology to produce a document that adds no value in its context. With appropriate approval, the team drops it. Which process-tailoring action is this?
options: Added
Blended
Aligned
Removed
explanation: Process elements can be added, modified, removed, blended or aligned. Removing reduces unnecessary cost or effort.

q: What is a suitability filter?
options: A mandatory procedure that selects the project manager
A tool for removing defects from deliverables
A decision-making tool that helps a team judge whether a predictive, adaptive or hybrid approach fits best
A report listing all project risks
explanation: A suitability filter is not a rigid method but a decision-making tool that evaluates culture, team and project factors to support the choice of approach.

q: A project team wants to change a process in a way that will affect other departments. Whose approval may be required?
options: Nobody; teams may tailor anything freely without consulting others
The PMO, because the tailoring affects external groups
Only the newest team member
The customer's end users
explanation: Tailoring that only affects the project team usually needs the project manager's approval. Tailoring that affects external groups may need PMO approval.

q: Which statement about tailoring is correct?
options: It is a continuing activity, revisited at review points, phase gates and retrospectives
It is done once at the very start of the project and is never revisited after it has been approved
It is only permitted on adaptive projects
It should be done without involving the team
explanation: Tailoring is not a single, one-time exercise. Review points, phase gates and retrospectives provide opportunities to inspect and adapt.

q: A project's deliverables keep failing quality checks. According to the tailoring diagnostics, what is the best response?
options: Add several more inspection steps at the very end
Replace the whole team
Ignore it until the customer complains
Analyze the root causes and improve the process
explanation: The guidance is to analyze root causes and focus on process improvements rather than just increasing verification steps.

q: Which is a benefit of involving team members in tailoring the approach?
options: It removes the need for governance
It guarantees that the project finishes earlier than planned
It increases the team's commitment to the approach
It eliminates all project risk
explanation: Benefits of tailoring include more commitment from the team members who helped tailor, a stronger customer focus and more efficient use of resources.

q: A new project manager plans to "complete the Stakeholders domain in month one, the Schedule domain in month two and the Risk domain in month three". What is wrong with this plan?
options: Nothing; this is the order the Guide recommends
The domains run concurrently through the whole project, not in sequence
Risk must come first, because it carries the highest weighting of the seven domains
Only the Governance domain may be worked on in month one
explanation: The performance domains have no weighting or order. They run concurrently through the whole project and work as one integrated system, not as separate silos.

q: A team is proud of its 60-page schedule document, but no stakeholder reads it and nobody can say when value will be delivered. What does the "check results" idea say about this?
options: The document is valuable in itself, because the organization's methodology requires it
The document should be made longer and more detailed
The document should be approved by the PMO before use
An output is valuable only if it serves a higher-order outcome
explanation: Project management activities add no value by themselves. A schedule is valuable because it aligns stakeholders around when value will be delivered. Every output should serve a higher-order outcome.

q: A team of six works adaptively on an internal tool, with the product owner in the same room. How much governance does this project most likely need?
options: Lightweight
Comprehensive
None at all
The same as a large predictive project
explanation: Governance can be lightweight for adaptive work, moderate for hybrid, and comprehensive for large predictive projects. Too many processes is costly and wasteful; too few makes management ineffective.

q: A project produces a weekly status report and a weekly risk report for the same readers. The team combines them into one report that serves both purposes. Which tailoring action is this?
options: Added
Removed
Blended
Aligned
explanation: Processes can be added, modified, removed, blended or aligned. Blending combines elements for added value. Removing would mean dropping one of the reports altogether.

q: Team members wait several days for a manager's signature on every purchase, even for small items, and work stalls. Which tailoring suggestion fits this situation?
options: Add another approval step to make the process more rigorous
Authorize people to decide up to set value thresholds
Run a team-building event to improve collaboration
Use value stream mapping to reduce work in progress
explanation: For long delays waiting for approvals, the suggested tailoring is to authorize people to decide up to set value thresholds, so that small decisions do not queue for a signature.

q: A customer's contract requires a monthly earned value report in a set format. The team finds it heavy and wants to tailor it out. What applies?
options: The team may drop it, because tailoring is always the team's choice
The team may drop it if the project manager approves
The team may replace it with a verbal update
The contract mandates it, which limits what the team can tailor
explanation: Tailoring has limits: organizational policy or a contract may mandate a particular approach. The team tailors within those limits.

q: A project team chooses which scheduling software it will use, weighing what suits the work against what the licence costs. In the 7th edition's list of things that can be tailored, which one is this?
options: Engagement
Life cycle and development approach
Tools
Processes
explanation: The 7th edition lists five things to tailor: life cycle and development approach, processes, engagement, tools, and methods and artifacts. Selecting the software or equipment the team will use is tailoring the tools.
